title: Extension of scalars preserves $\Dctf$
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let
$\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be one of the coefficient maps listed in the blueprint unit
sk-prop-scalar-six, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ is
its ring of integers: a homomorphism $A\to B$ of finite admissible rings;
$\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$ for a finite extension $F/E$ inside
$\Qlb$; $\mathcal O_E\to E$; $E\to\Qlb$; a continuous map
$\mathcal O_E\to A$ to a finite admissible ring; or a composite of these.
The topological coefficient rings are regarded as condensed rings
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], finite rings as discrete
ones, and $K_{\Lambda'}=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}K$ is
[sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Use bounded constructible complexes of finite
Tor amplitude on the small pro-étale site [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].
Let $X$ be a standing scheme. Then:

1. Every object of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is obtained by finitely many shifts,
   extensions and direct summands from objects $a_!P$, where
   $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ is a locally closed immersion and $P$ is pro-étale locally on
   $S$ of the form $P_0\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}\Lambda_S$ for a bounded complex $P_0$ of
   finite projective $\Lambda(*)$-modules ("locally perfect").
2. For every locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ and every
   $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, if $P$ is locally perfect over $\Lambda$, then $P_{\Lambda'}$ is locally perfect over
   $\Lambda'$, and $a_!(P_{\Lambda'})\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$.
3. $K\mapsto K_{\Lambda'}$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$.

Here finite projective means finitely generated and projective
[def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module]; thus the
local complexes in (1) are perfect scalar-ring complexes [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].
Tensor with the scalar ring means tensor with its constant sheaf, as in
[det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. For $a=i\circ u$, with $u$ open into
the closure of $S$ and $i$ closed into $X$, $a_!$ denotes $i_*u_!$, using
[sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek, sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Here $i_*=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_i}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(i^{\Ab}_*)$ is the module pushforward: the underlying sheaf of $i_*M$ is $i^{\Ab}_*M$ and the coefficient action is restricted along $\eta_i$, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback].

proof.text:
Finite-coefficient generators. The standing $X$ is Noetherian:
apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to
$X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; the spectrum of a field is Noetherian.
For every finite admissible ring $A$, apply
[det-sf-flat-model-generation](3). It states that $\Dctf(X,A)$ is the
subcategory generated by $a_!L$ under shifts, extensions and direct summands,
where $L$ is locally constant with finite projective $A$-module stalks.
Such $L$ is locally the constant sheaf of that finite projective module,
which is a bounded finite projective scalar complex concentrated in degree
zero. These are the locally perfect generators required in (1). The closure
is generated by finitary operations, so every object has a finite
construction with these operations. This argument covers arbitrary finite
commutative $A$, not only the $\ell$-primary case.
The current generation statement specifies ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude. For finite discrete $A$ the coefficient ring $A_X=p_X^*\underline A$ is the constant sheaf of rings $A$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] identifies $\underline A$ with the sheafified constant ring on profinite sets, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] carries this monoidal isomorphism to the pulled-back ring on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (and on every $W\in X_{\mathrm{proét}}$); module categories are transported along it. This identification is also the one used in steps 5, 8 and 9 for finite coefficients. These are the finite-coefficient categories used here, and its $a_!=g_*j_!$ convention agrees with the statement above.

Integral generators. If $K\in\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)$, then
$K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by
[det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Apply
[det-lem-int-tensor-shriek](2): $K$ is a finite iterated extension of $a_!M$
whose restrictions are scalar extensions of bounded finite free
$\mathcal O_E$-complexes. These are among the generators of (1).
This uses only the inclusion $\Dctf\subseteq\Dbc$, not an identification
with a category defined using a tower or derived completeness.

Field generators. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, an input in $\Dctf$
is again bounded constructible. By
[det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-generation] it is obtained by finitely many
cones and shifts from $a_!L$ with $L$ lisse. By
[sk-lem-coefficient-heart] lisse means pro-étale locally finite free, hence
locally perfect with its model in degree zero. A cone is an extension after
rotating its distinguished triangle. This proves (1) at the field stages
(including $\mathbf Q_\ell$), and step 2 includes $\mathbf Z_\ell$
by taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

Change the local projective models. Write $R=\Lambda(*)$ and
$R'=\Lambda'(*)$. Choose a cover $W\to S$ with
$P|_W\simeq\Lambda_W\otimes_R P_0^\bullet$, $P_0^\bullet$ bounded finite
projective. Each $P_0^q$ is a retract of a finite free $R$-module: take a
surjection $R^m\to P_0^q$ from finitely many generators and split it by
projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Tensoring the two splitting
maps preserves their composite identity. Thus $\Lambda_W\otimes_R P_0^q$
is a retract of $\Lambda_W^m$. Tensoring any short exact sequence with
this retract gives a direct summand of its finite direct-sum sequence, so
it is exact; this is flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The same
splitting exhibits $R'\otimes_R P_0^q$ as a retract of $(R')^m$, hence
as a finite projective $R'$-module. The bounded flat complex is K-flat by
[lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. By
[sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] its derived change of coefficients
is computed termwise. Restriction commutes with this change by
[det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1), and ordinary tensor associativity gives
$$
P_{\Lambda'}|_W\simeq
\Lambda'_W\otimes_{\Lambda_W}(\Lambda_W\otimes_R P_0^\bullet)
\simeq\Lambda'_W\otimes_{R'}(R'\otimes_R P_0^\bullet).
$$
This proves local perfectness in (2), even when $A\to B$ is not flat.

Cohomology of a local model. For any coefficient stage $\Gamma$ in
the list, put $R=\Gamma(*)$. The functor $M\mapsto\Gamma_W\otimes_R M$
is exact. For finite $R$ it is the constant-sheaf functor; exactness follows
by sheafifying the sectionwise exact constant-presheaf sequence, using
[lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. If $R$ is a field, each short exact
sequence of $R$-modules splits and its image under this additive functor
still splits. For $R=\mathcal O_F$, exactness follows from the same
constant-sheaf exactness followed by the flat ring map of
[det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients](1), which applies on
every scheme $W$. Consequently, for a bounded finite projective scalar
complex $Q_0^\bullet$,
$$H^q(\Gamma_W\otimes_R Q_0^\bullet)
=\Gamma_W\otimes_R H^q(Q_0^\bullet).$$
The ring $R$ is Noetherian: for finite rings and fields this follows directly
from their ideals, and for $\mathcal O_F$ it follows from the principal-ideal
assertion in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](2). Its ideals are
finitely generated. Thus the cycles are finite by
[lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], their quotients $H^q(Q_0^\bullet)$
are finite, and these modules are finitely presented by
[lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation]. The displayed
cohomology therefore has finite constant local models.

source.place: (2) Local models, constructibility of local cohomology

proof.text:
Global bounds for a locally perfect complex. Let $Q$ be locally
perfect on a stratum $S$ with coefficient $\Gamma$. The underlying space of the Noetherian $X$ from step 1 has every subset
retrocompact [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Since $X$ is quasi-compact, the
locally closed subspace $S$ is quasi-compact. The immersion $S\to X$ is locally
of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2), so $S$ is locally
Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. Thus $S$ is Noetherian. It is also quasi-separated: the intersection of any two affine opens of $S$ is an open subspace of its Noetherian underlying space, hence is quasi-compact. Thus $S$ is qcqs before applying the constructibility definition below. Choose a finite affine open cover
$S=\bigcup_{\alpha=1}^t U_\alpha$ and a pro-étale cover
$\{W_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ trivializing $Q$. Apply the explicit covering
condition of the current [sk-def-pe-site] over each $U_\alpha$: choose
finitely many affine opens
$V_{\alpha j}\subset W_{i(\alpha,j)}\times_S U_\alpha$ whose images cover
$U_\alpha$. Thus the finitely many $V_{\alpha j}$ together cover $S$, and $\{V_{\alpha j}\to S\}$ is itself a covering of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$: $W_{i}\times_SU_\alpha$ is the open subscheme of $W_i$ over $U_\alpha$, so $V_{\alpha j}$ is an open subscheme of $W_{i(\alpha,j)}$ and $V_{\alpha j}\to S$ is weakly étale, the property being local on the source [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]; for an affine open $W\subset S$, each $U_\alpha\cap W$ is quasi-compact (an open subset of the Noetherian space $S$), hence a finite union of affine opens $W_k$, and $V_{\alpha j}\times_S W=\bigcup_k V_{\alpha j}\times_{U_\alpha}W_k$ is a finite union of affine schemes; finitely many affine opens of the finitely many $V_{\alpha j}$ therefore have images covering $W$, which is the covering condition of [sk-def-pe-site].
This uses the finite affine refinement condition, not finiteness of the
original index set $I$. Since $S$ is a scheme, the definition's explicit
scheme hypothesis is satisfied. For the restriction $f\colon V_{\alpha j}\to W_{i(\alpha,j)}$, use the canonical natural isomorphism of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]: module pullback is the lift of inverse image with coefficient action through $\alpha_f^{-1}$. Together with its ring isomorphism $f^{-1}\Gamma_W\cong\Gamma_{V_{\alpha j}}$, this identifies the restricted model with $\Gamma_{V_{\alpha j}}\otimes_{\Gamma(*)}Q_0^\bullet$ for the same scalar complex on $W_{i(\alpha,j)}$. This exact comparison retains the bounded scalar model; it does not require equality of the two functors. Only untwisted coefficients are used. The current admissible list includes every coefficient here, in particular the finite-subextension condensed $\Qlb$ fixed in the statement. Choose $r$ to be the minimum of
these finitely many models' lower term degrees and $s$ the maximum of
their upper term degrees; pad a zero scalar model with zero terms if needed. If $S$ is empty, take $r=s=0$. Restrictions are exact by
[sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], so step 5 and the sheaf axiom show
that $H^q(Q)=0$ outside $[r,s]$ and that its cohomology sheaves have the
finite constant local models of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model].
They are constructible on the single stratum $S$: in its own underlying space, $S$ is both open and closed and hence constructible, so the one-piece partition is a finite stratification of the qcqs scheme $S$ allowed by [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude](1). For every $\Gamma_S$-module
$N$, restriction commutes with derived tensor by
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Locally $Q\otimes^L N$
is the ordinary tensor of the model with $N$, since its terms are flat and
it is K-flat [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. That complex has no terms
outside $[r,s]$, hence no cohomology there. Vanishing can be checked on a
cover, so the same bound holds globally for every $N$.
By [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], $Q\in\Dctf(S,\Gamma)$.

source.place: (2) Local models, finite global cohomology and Tor bounds

proof.text:
Apply step 6 to $Q=P_{\Lambda'}$ from step 4. Check the scheme
hypotheses before applying the preservation theorem. Every inverse image
under $a$ of an affine open of $X$ is quasi-compact by the retrocompactness
argument in step 6. Thus $a$ is quasi-compact, and its local finite type
from step 6 makes it finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
The same definitions show $S$ is finite type over $k$: locally, a finite
type $k$-algebra followed by a finite type algebra is generated over $k$
by the two finite sets of generators, and $S$ is quasi-compact.
An immersion is a monomorphism: on its open/closed local factorization
[def-weil-closed-immersion], maps through the open factor uniquely,
and maps through a quotient ring factor uniquely. Hence $\Delta_a$ is
an isomorphism, so $a$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Moreover
$\Delta_{S/k}$ is the base change of $\Delta_{X/k}$ along $a\times_k a$
because $S\times_XS=S$. It is a closed immersion by
[lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], so $S$ is separated over $k$.
Thus both $S$ and $X$ are standing schemes and $a$ is separated of finite
type. For the factorization $a=i\circ u$ in the statement, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] defines the open factor as $u_!=u^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_u}$. Its underlying abelian sheaf is $u^{\Ab}_!M$, and it is exact. Thus applying it termwise to complexes preserves quasi-isomorphisms and gives the open factor in $a_!=i_*u_!$. For the closed factor, [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] defines $i_*=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_i}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(i^{\Ab}_*)$. Its underlying sheaf is $i^{\Ab}_*M$ and its coefficient action is through $\eta_i$. Consequently the composite here is precisely the module extension by zero $i_*u_!$ fixed in the statement, for the same commutative condensed coefficient $\Lambda'$. Now [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images](2) carries
$Q\in\Dctf(S,\Lambda')$ to $a_!Q\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$.
This proves the remaining assertion of (2).

Retracts at finite coefficients. Let $C\in\Dctf(X,B)$ for a
finite admissible ring $B$, and suppose $J$ is a retract of $C$ in the
ambient derived category. The equivalence in
[det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] gives an étale bounded
constructible finite-Tor complex $C_0$ with $\nu_X^*C_0\simeq C$.
Here $B$ is Noetherian and the standing $X$ is qcqs. The exact fully faithful
functor of [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] identifies
$H^q(C)$ with $\nu_X^*H^q(C_0)$ and lifts its idempotent whose image is
$H^q(J)$ to an endomorphism of $H^q(C_0)$. Its image is constructible by
[thm-constructible-serre] (image equals kernel of the cokernel).
Exactness of $\nu_X^*$ identifies its image with $H^q(J)$. Since $X$ is qcqs and $B$ is a discrete Noetherian ring, [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] states that $\nu_X^*$ carries constructible étale sheaves of $B$-modules into $\Cons(X,B)$, so $H^q(J)\in\Cons(X,B)$; it vanishes outside the finite cohomological range of $C$. Thus $J$ has
bounded constructible cohomology. Tensoring the retraction with any module
still gives a retraction, so the Tor interval of $C$ bounds that of $J$.
It follows that $J\in\Dctf(X,B)$.

Thickness at the other coefficients and closure under triangles.
For $\mathcal O_F$, [det-lem-int-integral-heart-triangulated](2) explicitly
states that ambient kernels and cokernels of maps of constructible sheaves
are constructible. For fields the same is
[sk-lem-coefficient-heart](1). Hence an idempotent on a constructible sheaf
has constructible image (the kernel of its complementary idempotent).
Cohomology of a derived retract is such an image, so it is bounded
constructible. The Tor bound passes to a retract as in step 8.
For finite coefficients, [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] states
triangulation of the bounded constructible category for every finite
commutative ring. For integral coefficients this is
[det-lem-int-integral-heart-triangulated](1), and for fields it is
[det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated]. Finally
[det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] states the shift, triangle and
retract closure of finite Tor amplitude. Intersecting these properties
with bounded constructibility, and using step 8 for finite coefficients,
shows that $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$ is thick at every stage.

source.place: (3), thickness at integral and field coefficients and Tor closure

proof.text:
Exact scalar extension and generation. The actual derived
extension of scalars along $\Lambda_X\to\Lambda'_X$ is an exact
triangulated functor by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2), applied to
the small ringed pro-étale site. It therefore preserves shifts and
extensions. It also preserves retracts: if $pi=1$, then $T(p)T(i)=1$.
Step 7 verifies that each generator immersion has both schemes in the standing separated finite-type setting, as required by the current [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](2). Its exact locally closed extension by zero is applied termwise to the unbounded ambient complexes, and all scalar tensors here are ordinary derived tensors without completion. By that clause, the image of each generator $a_!P$
is $a_!(P_{\Lambda'})$, which belongs to $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$ by steps 4–7.
Steps 8–9 show that the inverse image of this target subcategory is closed
under the finite operations in (1). Inducting on the finite construction
in steps 1–3 proves (3) for each elementary map. For a composite of listed
maps, apply this result successively and identify the composite functor
with extension along the composite by
[det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](3). The local calculation in step 4 applies
to that composite as well, so all three clauses hold as stated.

split_report.summary: Expanded the coefficient list and local-model conventions without changing the three assertions, and split the proof into finite/integral/field generation, local projective scalar change, finite-cover cohomological and Tor bounds, extension by zero, thickness, and finite induction. All inputs are existing DAG nodes. This return-L repair revalidates the module pushforward/pullback against its current statement and source, writes its closed-factor scalar-restriction formula in step 7, and adds the exact pushforward-clause citation. Current scalar-pullback hypotheses and integral-heart coefficient conventions are checked explicitly; existing steps 7 and 10 verify the standing schemes and ordinary derived-tensor convention. All direct dependency statements and every step citation were reread and checked against the current DAG before the authoritative no-push dry run. No new node or Mathlib leaf is introduced.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–3 realize (1) Generators; steps 4–7 realize (2) Local models including the final a_! assertion; steps 8–10 supply thickness and generator induction for (3), and step 10 handles composites.
